In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the differentiation of primary keratinocytes involves the dynamic assembly of protein complexes with a core set of stable components, which is accompanied by the addition of dynamic components.
the assembly of complexes is dynamic and that this dynamic is not necessarily reflected by a dynamic gene expression.
the differentiation of human keratinocytes involves the assembly and disassembly of a number of complexes, with a large proportion of complexes being composed of dynamic proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the time-dependent assembly and disassembly of protein complexes is a fundamental mechanism in the regulation of cell fate decisions.
protein complexes can be assembled in a time-dependent fashion, with the majority of complexes containing both non-dynamic and time specific dynamic components.
the assembly of complexes during cell differentiation may be more dynamic than previously thought.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that the assembly of protein complexes can be a major contributor to cellular differentiation.
the assembly of complexes can be a dynamic process that is guided by competition between proteins.
we can now use the wealth of information available in public data repositories to understand the molecular mechanisms of cell differentiation.
